clean_body: As one of Nella’s best supporters, I wanted to make sure you saw the latest numbers. | Peter -- this is for your eyes only. As Nella Domenici’s campaign manager, I’ve been closely monitoring our internal polling numbers. We’re on a pathway to victory here in New Mexico , but I wanted to share an inside look at what we’re seeing. I’ll be frank-- We risk our opponent outspending us and controlling the message on TV. He’s a 20-year incumbent who has stacks of campaign cash, while Nella is a first-time candidate who is personally investing in this race. Nella is running because she wants better for New Mexico and feels, just as we all do, that Martin Heinrich is failing us. Peter, here are the key takeaways: State of the Race: New Mexico Senate 1. This is a resource campaign. Ad spending will dramatically affect the outcome of this race. If we are underfunded, it will give the Democrats a leg up. 2. There are a large number of “undecideds” in this race, and they favor Nella. It’s now up to us to convert undecided voters to Nella. 3. Heinrich has no room to grow. More New Mexicans know who he is and know he has failed to perform. More New Mexicans agree (45%-34%) that “Martin Heinrich has failed New Mexico.” 4. While Democrats are seeing a honeymoon phase after Joe Biden’s announcement of dropping out, Nella has not only held her numbers, but actually improved among Republicans without sacrificing appeal to Independent voters. Now, I am going to ask you to bet on New Mexico. There are so many critical races, We aren’t seeing the national attention on this Senate race, so your support today goes that much further. A TV ad running in Albuquerque will cost almost $750,000 less than the same ad running in Phoenix – and a Senate seat counts the same here, or anywhere in the country. That’s why your investment here can truly have an outsized impact on this election. With your support, we can flip this seat and retire Martin Heinrich for good. Thanks, Noah Jennings Campaign Manager, Nella for Senate | ABOUT NELLA New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years. Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant. Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans. Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. We believe in the power of education, not just for our kids, but for our families and our communities and the entire state. It’s also what empowers us as a nation,” Indiana is One of the Least Worker Friendly States The nongovernmental organization Oxfam released a new report this week that ranked the best and worst states in the U.S. to work, placing Indiana at number 33 in the nation. Though 30 states plus D.C. have raised their minimum wage requirements from the federally mandated $7.25 an hour, Indiana is one of the few that has failed to do so. body:
Voter Action Project Logo [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-weekly?refcode=090624_3&amount=25]
Folks:
Listen, the honest truth is: Felony disenfranchisement laws have a shameful history dating back to Jim Crow – and were never intended to target wealthy, powerful people. These laws were expressly written to make it harder for someone who had ever committed a crime to vote, even if they had repaid their debt to society.
These laws impact 4.4 million ordinary Americans currently disenfranchised by felony convictions and unable to vote.
The Inclusive Democracy Act would end this blatant double standard , restoring full voting rights for federal elections to all Americans with felony convictions, and ensuring NO American is denied their right to have a say in our democracy.
Sign our petition now: Tell Congress it's time to end shameful double standards in our legal system >> [https://act.commoncause.org/letters/tell-congress-end-shameful-double-standards-in-our-legal-system?source=090224swap-ifvap&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
SIGN HERE NOW ⇨ [https://act.commoncause.org/letters/tell-congress-end-shameful-double-standards-in-our-legal-system?source=090224swap-ifvap&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
Why are we talking about a double standard? One huge example:
Despite his 34 felony convictions, Donald Trump doesn’t have to worry about his eligibility to vote this fall. He has the wealth, connections, and privilege to ensure his voting rights would never be in question – not to mention a high-powered legal team paid for by his political donors due to gaps in campaign finance laws.
Just look at Trump’s home state of Florida, where Governor Ron DeSantis has personally guaranteed that the former president will be able to cast a ballot this fall. In stark contrast, Black Florida residents have been dragged from their homes at gunpoint and arrested for the "crime" of not realizing they were ineligible to vote .

There’s not much worse in Democratic politics than those alarmist fundraising emails.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20240906&t=1&akid=1149%2E587540%2EDjvxNR)
Peter,
There’s not much worse in Democratic politics than those alarmist fundraising emails that make it sound like the world’s going to end tomorrow if you don’t give them thousands of dollars _right now_. Especially the ones that offer an “800% MATCH!” that doesn’t actually exist — is that even legal?
It’s really important to me that our email program at Leaders We Deserve be the complete opposite of that. **I want to make sure supporters like you feel like we’re respecting your time, attention, and contributions. Not like you’re being treated like a bank.**
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240906?amount=5&refcode=em20240906-1149&refcode2=1149_587540_DjvxNR&akid=1149%2E587540%2EDjvxNR)**
It’s in our best interest too — because we don’t take corporate donations. We rely exclusively on the trust and generosity of donors like you to support our work to get more young candidates elected. And the quickest way to lose that trust (along with our ability to operate) would be to take your support for granted.
So when we send out fundraising appeals, we’ll _always_ be upfront about our goals and exactly what your money will go to support. Why would anyone trust an organization that _doesn’t_ operate that way?
**Right now, we’re supporting an incredible slate of 13 candidates running for Congress and state legislatures across the nation.** Every dollar we raise from emails like this goes directly to helping get those candidates elected.
That means things like ad buys in our candidates' districts to get the word out about their campaigns. Research and polling to give campaigns a solid idea of where they stand. Travel costs so our team can meet candidates and their staff to assess the campaign on the ground, in person. We do it all to help our endorsed candidates win.
**But we can’t do it without you, Peter. Like I said, we don't take _any_ corporate donations.**
**[So if you want to support our work to elect a new generation of candidates across the country, will you pitch in $5 or more to Leaders We Deserve today?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240906?refcode=em20240906&amount=5&refcode2=1149_587540_DjvxNR&akid=1149%2E587540%2EDjvxNR)**

Thanks so much for your support,
David Hogg

# Melton for Iowa 2024
---
---
| Hello Peter,

This is Ryan Melton, Democrat running for the U.S. House in Iowa's 4th Congressional District. During my 2024 campaign, I'll send you a weekly email to keep you in the loop while not overwhelming your inbox. Typically, the newsletter will be a review from the week prior: Where we went, what issues of note were on the minds of those I met with, where we'll be in the next week, etc.
Where I went on the campaign trail last week: Last week, I sat down for an hour-long interview with Julie Gammack (I'll post the audio link below), sat in on Arnie Arnesen's radio show and answered some questions about Iowa politics and Kevin Virgil's endorsement I received, chatted with students at Northwest Iowa Community College and Dordt University, spoke with folks in Marshalltown at Iowa State House Rep. Sue Cahill's fundraiser, and attended a Labor Day picnic in Fort Dodge.
The pressing issue on the campaign trail last week: Last newsletter, I went into detail on the unprecedented endorsement I received from Kevin Virgil, the Republican who ran in the primary against my general election opponent, Randy Feenstra. The endorsement has certainly been the number 1 thing folks have wanted to chat with me about since. It's given Democrats in our conservative district hope that progress can be made here too.
The Iowa GOP leadership wasn't too excited about Virgil endorsing me. In fact, they spent all of last week on social media publicly panicking about it, begging people to vote for Feenstra regardless, calling Virgil names like "sore loser" (that was Gov. Reynolds), and calling me a "radical Democrat" who is a "Bernie Sanders Lover" (I certainly am a fan) as if that's a bad thing (it's not).
A number of folks, including journalists, were befuddled as to why the Iowa GOP sent out all its leaders, such as Gov. Reynolds, Reps. Miller Meeks, Nunn, Hinson, and Attorney General Brenna Bird among others, to amplify the story of Virgil's endorsement of me when one could argue it would've been better for them to ignore it and hope it didn't reach many Iowans. They amplified the story so much it landed in the New York Post.
I certainly was thinking the same thing, but came to the conclusion that the only logical explanation for all the free press and name recognition boost they gave was because they don't like what their internal polling numbers are showing them, and felt they had no other choice. In fact, last week, a Main Street USA/Florida Atlantic U. poll found Democrats are up in three of the four congressional districts in Iowa, and that poll was conducted before I received Virgil's endorsement. Also, despite Feenstra posting internal numbers at least twice regarding his primary race against Virgil on his campaign socials, he hasn't done that once in our general election race. Makes you wonder why.
What also was notable is if you read all of the social media posts submitted on the issue at hand by Iowa's GOP leaders, literally none of them addressed Virgil's critiques of what has happened in Iowa under GOP leadership that led him to endorse me. None rebutted his concerns (and mine) on the hollowing out of our rural communities, the cancer crisis, the decline of our public education rankings, or the sell out by Iowa GOP leadership of their rank and file voters to do the bidding of their big money corporate donors. Personally, if I was a Republican, reading my party leaders lecture and browbeat me to vote for them without addressing Virgil's concerns or acknowledging their role in the amplification of what ails this state that Virgil and I point out, I'd be even less likely to vote for them.
So, let's keep this momentum going. Spread the word. Share my newsletter emails. Put out my yard signs. Help us with post card writing. Donate if able. Depending on how you look at it (as there's redistricting of Congressional Districts every ten years), a Democrat hasn't won this U.S. House seat in roughly 40 years. I turn 40 this month. We have a unique opportunity here, so let's capitalize on it and create a better Iowa for all.

Now, we’re seeing a surge of grassroots momentum from Democrats across the country — and the energy on the ground here in Florida has been electric. With just 60 days left until the General Election, my team and I are doing everything we can, from traveling across the state to connect with voters to launching brand new TV ads — in English and Spanish — to fight back against Rick Scott's attack ads.
That's why I was so glad to discuss these major updates on Morning Joe to spread the word nationwide about how high the stakes are in Florida's elections.

_Friend, we absolutely cannot let him become the Senate majority leader this November._
**Make no mistake: Mitch McConnell's time as Senate GOP leader was one of the worst things to ever happen to the Senate.** It will take years for our country and our democracy to fully recover from his decades of corruption, cronyism, extremism, and obstruction.
_**But Rick Scott as Senate GOP leader would be much, much worse.**_
He's already spent over** $4 MILLION **running attack ads, and he can keep writing checks from his massive fortune of almost a quarter-billion dollars. Last time around, he spent **$64 million **of his own fortune to buy his seat.
**I'm not just up against an extremist, friend — I'm up against a _multi-millionaire_ extremist. body:
There are less than two months until Election Day.

|
#
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92316492/496712008/1135690821?refcode=AU_MKH_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20240906_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4Yjc2YjM4YS05OTZjLWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wic2K02ZQbDV5MSptHpIvMyZuG6jDHyi1Ouq-VhpP-Y=) Aloha Peter, It’s hard to believe it, but there are **less than two months until Election Day** — and that means I’m counting on grassroots supporters like you to step up and help me win re-election, protect our razor-thin Senate majority, and elect the Harris-Walz ticket this November. But before I ask for your support, let me explain why you’re guaranteed to make the greatest impact if you donate _right now:_
* It may not be November yet, but several key battleground states are set to begin early voting _this month_. We all know this election will come down to a handful of undecided voters, and every dollar will help us reach them before they cast their ballots.

* As we speak, Kamala Harris and Senate Democrats are making their final TV ad reservations in key battleground states. By chipping in now, you can help them match GOP spending and keep their ads on the air for as long as possible.

* And lastly, we’re required to report our final quarterly fundraising report before the election to the FEC on September 30th. body:
Our new plans

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92316562/496712337/-1463099547?refcode=-header-&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTNmOTUwNTEtOWE2Yy1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=eaMdXTdRTgTeppkXMKq1DlZn9zzVJaEVUhSdqqXWy9g=) | Hey Peter, I’m an organizer for Josh Harder and with ballots going out in California in less than 32 days, I thought now would be a good time to give you an inside look at our campaign and what’s been happening on the ground. **[If you can donate to support our field organizing efforts, I’ll put a link here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92316563/496712338/-1335305109?&refcode=E10359-20240906-FieldUpdate-SL-2024Race&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTNmOTUwNTEtOWE2Yy1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=eaMdXTdRTgTeppkXMKq1DlZn9zzVJaEVUhSdqqXWy9g=)** **[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92316564/496712339/-1335305109?&refcode=E10359-20240906-FieldUpdate-Image-2024Race&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTNmOTUwNTEtOWE2Yy1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=eaMdXTdRTgTeppkXMKq1DlZn9zzVJaEVUhSdqqXWy9g=)** We know who we need to talk with to win this election:
1. We have to talk to **persuadable voters** about why Josh is on their side. We know there are thousands of people who**** haven’t made their minds up yet and they have to hear from us before ballots drop.
2. We need to get in touch with voters who have historically been **disenfranchised from voting**. That means connecting authentically with our Latino community and energizing young voters to make their voices heard.

**We have to meet these voters where they are - in their neighborhoods and in their homes. That’s where our organizing program comes in. name: Tamie Wilson
subject: The Handmaid’s Tale was supposed to be fiction, not the ULTRA-MAGA blueprint
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP33/1/100067/images/LOGO.jpg]
Friends,
Here we are in 2024, and the plot of The Handmaid’s Tale is looking more like the Republican playbook than a cautionary tale.
ULTRA-MAGA leaders, from state houses to Congress, are making it clear: they want women silenced, subjugated, and stripped of our rights.
We’ve seen it time and time again—especially from their loudest mouthpieces.
JD Vance thinks women shouldn’t be allowed to divorce men who beat them and those who aren’t married and don’t have kids are “childless cat ladies” who shouldn’t have a voice.
Elon Musk chimed in by boosting a 4Chan post basically claiming he wants to go back to the colonial era when only “high-status males” (translation: land-owning white men) held political power.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20240906_handmaid_tale_image1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20240906_handmaid_tale_image1]
Donald Trump , as always, has unleashed his vitriol on women who’ve credibly accused him of sexual assault, calling them “liars” and attacking them personally. He also brags about being responsible for overturning Roe , and he believes women who have abortions should be punished.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20240906_handmaid_tale_image2 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20240906_handmaid_tale_image2]
And let’s not forget the Lt. Governor in North Carolina (and GOP nominee for governor this year), who said he “absolutely wants to go back” to the time before women had the right to vote. Yes, really.
But wait—it gets worse. States like Texas and South Carolina have floated the idea of executing women who seek abortions. Execution!
That’s extremist rhetoric straight out of Gilead. But ladies and gentlemen – WE ARE NOT GOING BACK.
Every dollar you contribute to our campaign goes directly into fighting back against the GOP’s war on women. They’re using fear and hate to control our futures, but together, we can shut them down. Chip in now to make sure our voices are louder than their attacks! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20240906_handmaid_tale_link1]
Margaret Atwood said it best: “Men are afraid that women will laugh at them. Women are afraid that men will kill them.”
And ULTRA-MAGA’s actions show just how willing they are to push women to the brink to hold onto their power.
And we can’t overlook our conspiracy theorist-in-chief opponent, Jim Jordan.
He’s been leading the charge against women’s rights for years, voting against the Violence Against Women Act and refusing to support equal pay for women. Jordan has attempted to introduce his own abortion torture bill three times, and his fellow Republicans keep blocking it for being too extreme!
Jordan is a proud co-sponsor of the National Right to Work Act, which undermines protections for women in the workplace.
And let’s not forget his shameful silence as countless women bravely came forward to name Donald Trump as their abuser—because for Jim Jordan, power always matters more than justice.
The truth is, Republicans know exactly what they’re doing.
They’re using fear and hate to control the narrative and keep women from fighting back.
But here’s the thing—they see us fighting for our rights, and it terrifies them.
They know that when women rise up, we are unstoppable, and that’s why they’re desperate to hang on to power.
I am making amazing progress in the district. The energy for this campaign is amazing. I wish you all were here to feel it.
So, let’s double down and keep the pressure on. We’ve got the power, we’ve got the momentum, and with your support, we can stop this dystopian nightmare from becoming reality. We need you to dig deep and give big today. We’re busy buying ads so we can make sure everyone learns the truth about Jordan and what he doesn’t do for them. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tamie-wilson-for-us-c2g?refcode=20240906_handmaid_tale_link2]
Working for US,
Tamie Wilson

| **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: It’s happening
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
Conservative, crypto-backed groups are spreading misinformation to buy this Senate seat

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2333%2E4032634%2Eru-Bsz)
---
It’s happening. Now that we’re in the general election here in Massachusetts, we just discovered that conservative, crypto-funded groups are starting to place six-figure ad buys against me — spreading misinformation to voters to prop up my Republican opponent. Some of the funders behind those ads are crypto investors like the Winklevoss brothers — Yes those guys from _The Social Network_ — because they’re upset that I’ve called for fair regulations around the industry that protect working people. This is a strategy that continues across the country: Powerful special interests use their giant piles of money to influence elections by buying onslaughts of advertising against candidates who threaten their bottom line. **We’ve got to stop this from happening in Massachusetts because the Senate majority — and the future of abortion rights — could be decided by _a single seat_. And these far-right and rich special interests are trying to buy this one to tilt power in their favor.** Look, I’m sick of the outsized influence of special interest money in elections. I’m fighting to end this corrupt system where our democracy is sold to the highest bidder. But first, we’ve got to fight back and defeat these special interests targeting us. Now that we’re in the general election here in Massachusetts, we just discovered that conservative, crypto-funded groups are starting to place six-figure ad buys against me — spreading misinformation to voters to prop up my Republican opponent. This is a strategy that continues across the country: Powerful special interests use their giant piles of money to influence elections by buying onslaughts of advertising against candidates who threaten their bottom line. We’ve got to stop this from happening in Massachusetts because the Senate majority — and the future of abortion rights — could be decided by a single seat. And these far-right and rich special interests are trying to buy this one to tilt power in their favor. Look, I’m sick of the outsized influence of special interest money in elections. I wanted to reach out, personally, to explain exactly why I entered this race. **[If you don’t have time to read the rest of my note (that’s okay!), can I count on you to pitch in a few dollars to our grassroots campaign before you click away?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/92318564/496719058/476240536?refcode=em_fr_2024.09.06_b2_jb_all-nd&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY3MjEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjZhZjUwNjMtYTA2Yy1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=q3g2KsMMuodGC-RMdn3kF1EC7wr2VYPeP8u2LheSzKQ=)** I grew up in a working-class family. Both of my parents were teachers and there were times when it felt impossible to get ahead. I know a lot of families today can relate. **Despite doing everything right, countless families across America just can’t seem to get ahead. ** **I’m running for Congress because our community deserves a Congresswoman who’s not afraid to stand up to anyone to ensure Oregonians get ahead.** We need leaders who will stand up to far-right extremists, and deliver meaningful change for families across Oregon. Peter, even if Donald Trump loses, the extreme principles laid out in Project 2025 will live on in the states. The extremist plan is already taking hold in states across the country, and its adherents will work to keep the plan marching forward. **Let’s take a look at just how Project 2025’s anti-democracy, anti-freedom agenda is being implemented by MAGA Republicans in Arkansas, right now: **
* This November, voters will _not_ get the chance to vote on an abortion rights ballot initiative.
* The far-right secretary of state rejected the abortion rights team’s ballot petition signatures, saying organizers didn’t correctly submit a paid canvasser training certification.
* In a 4-3 decision, the state supreme court said that the secretary of state unequally applied laws around paid canvassers, but the justices refused to check that and right the wrong.
* In the minority dissent, one justice said “the majority has succeeded in its efforts to change the law in order to deprive the voters of the opportunity to vote on this issue, which is not the proper role of this court.”
* MAGA Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders said she’s “proud” that she built the conservative court majority that ushered this decision through.

Project 2025 is a blueprint to dismantle our rights and overrule the will of the people. Arkansas is just one state where pieces of that plan are already being rolled out, and **health care and reproductive rights for everyone in Arkansas will suffer as a result. And we are seeing this across the country, with 22 states enacting abortion bans since _Roe_ was overturned.** [**Your gift today is a commitment to elect candidates who will hold the line for our freedoms and democracy. Systemic racism in our policing imposes a dangerous and disparate impact on how law enforcement addresses gun violence based on the the skin color. While legacy media is largely complicit in enabling this disparate impact, the impact itself is fatal for Black and brown communities. We must actively counter it to uphold true justice and security. **Let 's Address This.**
**Let's Address This with Qasim Rashid is a reader-supported publication. Consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..xvQvQYdgWvClnd4VlN3dC4gN5z8j9crsBJL-ple-LrA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=148590989)
## A disturbing trend
Think about this.
In Apalachee High School, Georgia, Colt Gray murdered 4 people--he was arrested alive and unharmed.
In Atlanta, Georgia, Robert Aaron Long murdered 8 people while ostensibly targeting Asian Americans--he was arrested alive and unharmed.
In Charleston, South Carolina, Dylan Roof targeted a Black church and murdered 9 people--he was arrested alive and unharmed. The officers even took him to Burger King after his mass murder.
In Buffalo, New York, Payton Gendron targeted a grocery store in a Black neighborhood and murdered 10 people--he was arrested alive and unharmed.
In Aurora, Colorado, James Holmes murdered 12 people--he was arrested alive and unharmed.
In Parkland, Florida, Nikolas Cruz murdered 17 people--he was arrested alive and unharmed.
In El Paso, Texas, Patrick Crusius murdered 23 people while targeting Latinos--he was arrested alive and unharmed.
Each of the aforementioned white mass shooters committed mass murder in broad daylight--often targeting Black, Latino, and Asian communities. And despite being heavily armed, each mass murderer was arrested alive. Meanwhile Black Americans Tamir Rice, Aiyana Jones, Breonna Taylor, George Floyd, Eric Garner--all unarmed and innocent of any wrong doing--were killed immediately by law enforcement.
The question is not to ask why didn't law enforcement also kill white mass shooters, but rather, why won't law enforcement exercise the same restraint on unarmed Black people, that they exercise on armed white mass murderers? And while some may critique my observation as anecdotal, the data proves this racism is systemic.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..xvQvQYdgWvClnd4VlN3dC4gN5z8j9crsBJL-ple-LrA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=148590989)
## Data confirms you're not imagining the racism
A comprehensive study by The Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) published in the medical journal _The Lancet_ reviewed 30 years of medical data on police violence. They report [both the exponential rate of Americans killed by law enforcement, and the disproportionate rate of Black Americans killed by law enforcement](https://substack.com/redirect/451873b6-f35b-45ae-a554-e30de8d29f20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> According to the study, between 1980 and 2018 there were about 30,000 deaths from [police violence](https://substack.com/redirect/8e73cd61-db28-4808-81cd-73f60de8765a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) across the country. On average, that's the equivalent of 2 people in the U.S. being killed by police officers every single day. _Researchers also found that Black Americans were as much as 3.5 times more likely to die from police violence than white Americans_. Though other studies in the past have found similar rates of under-reporting and racial disparities, the IMHE's report is the most expansive with regards to the timeframe covered.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..xvQvQYdgWvClnd4VlN3dC4gN5z8j9crsBJL-ple-LrA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=148590989)
## Media remains complicit in elevating racism
And even when Black people are victims of mass shootings or police violence, media often demonizes them as villains. Consider this most recent case of the Apalachee high school shooting. Colt Gray, who is white, was the shooter. Yet [@wsbtv](https://substack.com/redirect/dde148e4-72fb-482d-9e8d-706f71bb4649?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tweeted to their 1.2 million followers a photo of Mason Schermerhorn--the Black child who was murdered--with the caption, "_A 14-year-old suspect, Colt Gray, was arrested_."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fd84bddd-1c6a-4e30-aa8f-cc1c58be39e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And again, far from anecdotes, the data shows that media's characterization of Black people is consistently mortifying. A recent study by Color of Change, a racial justice organization, and Family Story, an advocate of diverse family arrangements [reports that](https://substack.com/redirect/e72b900e-c3a8-485c-9b78-e0918383d1f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),
> Major media outlets routinely present a distorted picture of black families -- portraying them as dependent and dysfunctional -- while white families are more likely to be depicted as sources of social stability.
No doubt you have personally seen examples of this media bias throughout instances of police violence against Black people. After police officer Darren Wilson killed Michael Brown the New York Times described Brown as "[No angel](https://substack.com/redirect/95c11310-cc81-4412-bfec-2438ff906ff9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." After George Zimmerman cosplayed a cop and murdered Trayvon Martin, media relentlessly reminded everyone that Martin smoked marijuana. After police officer Timothy Loehmann murdered 12-year-old Tamir Rice, police and media described Rice as "[A thug](https://substack.com/redirect/b1dfda26-7a9b-432f-8012-09e640337473?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." In each case media went out of their way to further dehumanize an already murdered Black child. This is sadly one way legacy media continues to enable and perpetuate white supremacy in the public discourse.
## In Conclusion
As I've written before, the solution to these injustices are [comprehensive gun safety laws](https://substack.com/redirect/6b4d753d-8571-486e-ba37-483ece9ab632?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [meaningful police reform](https://substack.com/redirect/8ad04311-55b0-4c72-8320-ab9af3405a83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and holding legacy media accountable. The injustices emboldened and perpetuated in our current systems are a painful reminder that a system cannot fail those it was never meant to protect in the first place. We must challenge this injustices and build better systems on the tenets of justice. Only then can we ensure future generations do not suffer the same cycles of violence that continue to devastate our nation today.

name: Jill Stein
subject: Israel murdered an American today.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jill Stein for President 2024
body:
“They killed her. They shot her in the head. For what?”

| | | [ ](https://www.jillstein2024.com/?e=e813143e1dc0d3b0ffcb007ffe357333&utm_source=jillsteinforpresident&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=west_bank&n=1)
---
Peter,

She was 26 years old. She recently graduated from the University of Washington in Seattle.

She was like millions of our daughters and nieces and sisters – her whole life ahead of her. But now Aysenur Eygi is dead – murdered by Israel today in the West Bank.
---
---
I am sickened. I am heartbroken. I am disgusted and outraged. And you should be, too.

Today the Israeli Occupation Forces brutally murdered Aysenur – an American citizen and a peace activist protesting settlements in the West Bank.

Israeli forces shot her in the head. Deliberately. Just as they did Shireen Abu Akleh two years ago.

Mainstream media is already working overtime to whitewash this crime.

They’ve described Aysenur as a “Turkish-American” or “American-Turkish” in **an obvious attempt to downplay her identity as a full American citizen** (not that her citizenship should matter ... but to our policymakers and the public, it does).

They’ve called it “a shooting” stating that “an activist was killed” without describing how she died – or by whose hand.

This is important. Do not look away. This is what witnesses had to say:
---
---
Just after graduation this year, Aysenur joined a group of activists with the International Solidarity Movement, going directly to the heart of danger to hold the line as a peace activist against illegal Israeli “settlements” in the West Bank.

That’s where she was today when, unprovoked, IDF soldiers murdered her in cold blood with a killshot directly to the head.

Biden administration officials like Anthony Blinken can wring their hands and cluck their tongues and “condemn” the horrific violence playing out every single day against Palestinians and peace activists in every part of Palestine (NOT just Gaza).

But those protestations ring hollow when the same people shaking their heads with regret and dismay are rubber-stamping the latest billion-dollar-arms shipment to the murderers pointing the gun.

Aysenur Eygi was a brilliant young woman who dedicated her life to the service of others. As a fresh graduate she could have been chasing the career of her dreams. But she chose to hold the line for Palestine.

In February of this year, following the death of three American soldiers in Jordan at the suspected hands of Iranian-backed proxy rebels, Joe Biden forcefully declared: _“If you harm an American, we will respond."

_**Well Joe. They murdered an American today. Will you finally stop arming the murderers?

****The truth is Biden won’t seek justice for Aysenur because he knows that ultimately, he is responsible.** By arming this fascist, murderous, apartheid regime and giving them unrestricted political cover, he may as well have loaded the gun.

**Aysenur will not rest until we end our support for this violent regime.

** As your president, I will terminate all arms transfers and military aid to Israel on DAY ONE of my administration. I will impose an arms embargo until the Israeli government joins the peace process as a legitimate partner and an honest broker. And I will support international arrest warrants for Netanyahu and his cabinet of thugs.

**Biden called Israel’s planned assault on Rafah a “red line.”** Israel ignored the United States, ignored the international community, and invaded Rafah with a devastating military assault. **And**** _nothing_****happened.

** Now they’ve murdered an American citizen – and still nothing is happening.

It ends with us.

In solidarity,

Jill

name: Nick Begich
subject: It's about ALASKAN jobs
body:
Alaskans are working for work, but Mary Peltola wants to bring in more foreign workers? | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
## Prioritizing Jobs for Alaskans First!

Dear Friends,

I want to take a moment to respond to some recent comments from my opponent, Mary Peltola. As you may have seen, she’s calling for more foreign workers to fill jobs here in Alaska, while her allies are running ads attacking me for running an international business. The irony is hard to miss.

Here’s the truth: I’ve spent my career building businesses that create jobs, both in Alaska and across the U.S. In fact, I've specialized in working with startups with nothing but a PowerPoint deck and a dream. Today, I'm proud to say that many of those companies went on to create hundreds and in some cases thousands of new U.S. jobs. Additionally - and you won't see this in the Democrat ads - **my businesses in Alaska directly employ more than 100 RURAL Alaskans**. Unlike Mary, who has never employed an Alaskan and who is now advocating to bring in more foreign workers to Alaska, my priority is to make sure Alaskans—our friends, neighbors, and families—are the ones filling those jobs.

Our state faces a real problem right now: people are leaving, and too many Alaskans are struggling to find opportunities. With thousands of qualified Alaskans looking for work, it’s time we focus on getting them the jobs they deserve. That should be the top priority of anyone working to represent Alaska.

At a time when our population is shrinking and our unemployment rate is still too high, we don’t need more foreign workers coming to Alaska to take jobs that should go to Alaskans. We need to invest in our workforce, in our communities, and in creating opportunities that allow people to build their lives right here in our state. That’s what I’m fighting for, and I’m grateful to have your support as we work to make it happen.

**Thank you, from the bottom of my heart, for standing with us.** Let’s keep this momentum going and take back Alaska’s seat in Congress!

Together, we can ensure a prosperous future for all Alaskans.

**America First, Fighting for Alaska!**

Onward to victory,

Nick Begich
Candidate for U.S. Congress

Our state faces a real problem right now: people are leaving, and too many Alaskans are struggling to find opportunities. With thousands of qualified Alaskans looking for work, it’s time we focus on getting them the jobs they deserve. That should be the top priority of anyone working to represent Alaska. At a time when our population is shrinking and our unemployment rate is still too high, we don’t need more foreign workers coming to Alaska to take jobs that should go to Alaskans. We need to invest in our workforce, in our communities, and in creating opportunities that allow people to build their lives right here in our state. That’s what I’m fighting for, and I’m grateful to have your support as we work to make it happen. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart, for standing with us.
